question.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-2<x<0,\,0<y<-x\}.
$$

The interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-2<x<0,\,\bbox[5px,border:1px solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}}\,\}.
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14245698/assets/4073e99607c1e824f67b24bc93955b39c5b320901cd391ff3adb51444d1e1416.png)

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14245698/assets/79e005cc03bb625657c652324db58db653882c640e94ea4b21a386676745bd14.png)

So, in this case, the interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-2<x<0,\,0<y<-x\}.
$$
